text: Unlike the Beginner project's flat CSV, the ticketing API exports one JSON document per ticket event — a ticket being opened, or later updated with a new status or a refund. Landing that correctly is where this pipeline actually starts.

Here's one real export line. Ticket ID, subscriber ID, category, priority, status, when it was opened, and a refund amount. Notice refund_amount is null on most rows in a real export, because most tickets never involve a refund at all — Finance's view, a few lessons from now, only cares about the rows where it isn't.

The standard, reliable Snowflake pattern is to land semi-structured data exactly as the source sent it, before extracting a single field. One column, raw_payload, typed VARIANT — Snowflake's native type for JSON. A change in the source shape later only affects the parsing step, never this load step.

Loading it is the same real COPY INTO command this capstone already uses for CSV loads, with one difference: FILE_FORMAT equals TYPE JSON instead of TYPE CSV. Snowflake reads each JSON object and inserts it as one row's raw_payload value, with no flattening or guessing. ON_ERROR ABORT_STATEMENT means one malformed line fails the whole load loudly, instead of silently vanishing.
With the raw JSON safely landed, next lesson pulls real fields out of it — ticket ID, status, refund amount — using Snowflake's actual VARIANT parsing syntax.
